stem.text: Solid sulfur consists of molecules made up of eight atoms covalently bonded together.
The bonding in sulfur dioxide is $\text{O=S=O}$.
enthalpy change of combustion of $\text{S}_8$, $\Delta H_{\text{c}}^{\ominus}\,\text{S}_8\text{(s)} = -2376\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
energy required to break 1.0 mol $\text{S}_8\text{(s)}$ into gaseous atoms = $2232\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
Using these data, what is the value of the $\text{S=O}$ bond enthalpy?
